claims.text: Wheat-based baked goods (shortcakes, baked donuts, baked sweets) are produced and displayed alongside the macarons in a shared patisserie environment.
Products rely on eggs, butter, dairy and chocolate; the signature macaron is made with Hokkaido butter and Belgian chocolate, so cross-contact with animal ingredients is pervasive.

name: 囲炉裏ダイニング たなか (Irori Dining Tanaka)

claims.text: Menus include organic vegetable salads and platters of fresh Yamato-grown country vegetables, so there are some plant-based side options on the table.

name: イタリア食堂 パインストア (Italia Shokudo Pine Store)

claims.text: Menu is built around pork ham, smoked mackerel, and cheese, and even a vegetable dish (mushroom stir-fry) uses a fermented mushroom dashi, so vegetable plates are not reliably plant-based.

name: ゐざさ茶屋（ゐざさ中谷本舗 東大寺門前夢風ひろば店） (Izasa Chaya (Izasa Nakatani Honpo, Todaiji M)

claims.text: No gluten-free soy sauce is documented; standard sushi/fish seasoning uses wheat-based soy sauce, and the menu also includes wheat sōmen and tempura.
The core kakinoha-zushi is naturally a rice-and-fish dish wrapped in a persimmon leaf, so it contains no wheat in the wrapping or rice itself.

Dishes use house-made soy sauce and miso made from Daiteppo heirloom soybeans; Japanese soy sauce and miso of this kind typically contain wheat, so the menu should be assumed to contain gluten unless confirmed otherwise.
This is a dedicated wild-game restaurant where the entire menu is meat-based; there are no vegan or vegetarian dishes documented.

name: 純喫茶シンロク×オーシマドーナツ奈良店 (Junkissa Shinroku x Oshima Donut Nara)

claims.text: The shop fries wheat-based donuts on site; no gluten-free menu or dedicated equipment is documented, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
All products are plant-based and described as suitable for vegan diets, built around organic persimmon-leaf tea and persimmon-leaf powder rather than animal ingredients or fish dashi.
Persimmon leaves are grown without pesticides on the company's own organic-certified farm, with cultivation through to product carried out consistently in-house.

name: 柿の葉ずし 平宗 奈良店 (Kakinohazushi Hiraso Nara-ten)

claims.text: Menu pairs sushi with wheat-based somen/nyumen and tempura and uses soy sauce; no gluten-free protocol is documented, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used with the sushi and dishes; no tamari/GF soy sauce is mentioned.
Signature dishes use fish (mackerel/salmon) and fish-based dashi broths; sesame tofu and tea porridge appear on set menus but are not offered as a verified vegan course.
